### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b31d90fb37d490d7da12c7acd4b14c4feb22501` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `35c40cd6419eb0655e2b1f6191af5ecb27a8b140` — the merge of head `9897eaae2913a6e7e6581b84de95a82eb07369df` into base `0b31d90fb37d490d7da12c7acd4b14c4feb22501`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 35c40cd6419eb0655e2b1f6191af5ecb27a8b140 && git checkout 35c40cd6419eb0655e2b1f6191af5ecb27a8b140
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b31d90fb37d490d7da12c7acd4b14c4feb22501 9897eaae2913a6e7e6581b84de95a82eb07369df && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b31d90fb37d490d7da12c7acd4b14c4feb22501 && git merge --no-ff 9897eaae2913a6e7e6581b84de95a82eb07369df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b31d90fb37d490d7da12c7acd4b14c4feb22501
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: 110/110 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `270d9f4b351e2d75858876e959c7af6ea13adae2`

### ① Derived judgments

- Evidence base: card #18836 body, the PR body, the dev's `os-dev-report` (read only as the source of its flags), the diff `36583e989b..270d9f4b35`, rules read from `origin/main` with `git show`, and my own builds and ablations under `scratchpad/pr-18876/`. The card-comment fetch also returned the dispatching seat's claim comment (5724468860) and its review reply (5724759924); both are seat conclusions, were excluded as evidence, and nothing below rests on them.
- Criterion applied: SKILL.md:477 (does the card widen the accept set or expand the public surface), :513 and :515 (only the published contract surface counts), `references/lanes/spec.md:19-20`.
- Accept set: UNCHANGED. `POSITIONS` and `COLUMN_ENTRY_POSITIONS` are byte-identical between merge-base and head (the 163-line region diffed directly); the rule-file diff is 49 added, 0 removed lines, all placed after `COLUMN_ENTRY_POSITIONS`; `validateListViewFieldRefs`, both finding codes and both exported types are untouched; no `packages/spec` file, schema key, enum member, error code or registration is in the diff. The dev's "no POSITIONS row touched" is correct.
- Public surface: UNCHANGED, measured. `@objectstack/lint` ships `dist` only, `exports` is `.` and `./runtime`, `src/index.ts` has a 0-byte diff and re-exports the module by name (no `export *`), `src/runtime.ts` never references it. Built at merge-base and at head on the same dependency closure: 10 of 14 `dist/` artifacts (4 JS bundles, 6 `.d.ts`/`.d.cts`) are sha256-identical; `listViewWalkedPositions` reads 0 in all 14 files, 0 in `index.js`'s export clause, 0 in `index.cjs`'s `__export` map, 0 in every type file. Bright control `validateListViewFieldRefs`: 1/1 in the two entry listings, 2/2 in `index.d.ts`/`.d.cts`, 4/6/3/3 in the bundle bodies. Dark control `COLUMN_ENTRY_POSITIONS` (never exported): 2 in each bundle body, 0 in entries and types, so body presence is not a published entry. Instrument controls: adding the symbol to the barrel makes it read 1/1 in the entry listings and 2/2 in the types; the frozen-const shape reads 1 in each bundle body and 0 in the entries. The dev's "reaches no published entry, no type row" is correct.
- Four published files DID move: `index.js.map`, `index.cjs.map`, `runtime.js.map`, `runtime.cjs.map` (`sourcemap: true`, and `files[]` ships `dist` whole). Differing keys are `mappings` and `names` only; `sources` equal; the new symbol absent from `names`. A line-offset shift, not a surface, but the PR body's and the changeset body's "all nine dist artifacts byte-identical" is wrong on the count: 14 artifacts, 10 identical, 4 moved. Claim over-stated; ruling unaffected.
- Mechanical judges: `check-widening-tells` reads NOT MEASURED for all three files under either declaration (no declared surface covers `packages/lint`), and no `api-surface` baseline exists for `@objectstack/lint` (T3 covers `packages/spec/api-surface/*` only), so the build above is the only instrument that reads this package's public surface.
- Test-file and changeset edits: not published, no surface.
- Arm: the diff widens no accept set and expands no public surface ⇒ the declaration should carry `Clause-②: no`, with no direction arm (`no (widening)` is malformed per AGENTS.md:1068). The claim-time `yes (widening)` was the correct conservative floor for a new exported symbol (contract-review.md mechanical floor) and is not a fault (spec.md:20). Under `no`, `check-widening-tells --declaration no` exits 0 on this diff and the changeset level axis stands down.

### ② Semver level

- Declared: `@objectstack/lint: minor`. The `fixed` group lists about 70 packages including `@objectstack/lint` at 17.4.0, so this `minor` moves every one of them to 17.5.0.
- Delivered to consumers: 0 changed bytes in any code or type artifact; 4 source maps with shifted mappings; no new entry, no new type, no runtime change. Commit type `test(lint)`.
- Rule: AGENTS.md:1064-1068 says `yes` takes at least `minor`, so `minor` was consistent with the declared `yes` and the dev was right not to re-grade alone. With the arm ruled `no`, `pr-automation.yml` "WHICH LEVEL" governs: `minor` is for "a new exported symbol on an `index`, a new accepted key or value", none of which is here; "a fix( that changes no public surface stays patch"; route 2, "releases nothing (tests-only, and the like) ⇒ apply skip-changeset, PREFERRED; if you are unsure, take route 2".
- Ruling: `minor` is wrong. The grade should be `skip-changeset`: delete `.changeset/issue-18836-list-view-position-coverage.md` and apply the label. `patch` is the only other grade the rule admits (if the seat reads the four moved source maps as "publishes something"); it would still bump about 70 packages in lockstep for a map offset. Deleting the changeset also stops its inaccurate "all nine artifacts byte-identical" sentence reaching `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Level-axis consequence: with `Clause-②: no` in the PR body, `check-changeset-no-major` reads `not-declared` and exits 0 under either grade; the `edited` trigger re-fires Check Changeset on the body rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (declaration contradicted by measurement; A/B/C): A. Re-grade to `no`, delete the changeset, apply `skip-changeset`. Correction to its premise: dist is not wholly byte-identical (10 of 14; 4 maps moved); the answer stands because a map offset is neither a surface nor a release.
- `open_questions[1]` (set equality vs count equality): A, accept set equality as shipped. Verified: 57 rows across the two tables, 3 map to no position (the three hard-coded filter walks), 2 positions carry two rows each, covered set = walked set = 52; a count equality would have to hard-code those constants. The failing diff names the offender (`- "tree.ablationProbeField"`).
- Direction two (position added to the rule, no row): strictly stronger, verified. Base: 130 passed, 0 failed (silent). Head: 1 failed, `covers every position the rule walks`, naming `tree.ablationProbeField`.
- Direction one (position dropped from the rule): no regression, verified. Base and head both 1 failed, `views[0].list.tree.labelField reports at warning`, per-case; the head completeness assertion stays green exactly as the new comment says.
- Per-case assertions: unchanged, verified. The second table's `it` body is byte-identical; the measured describe differs only in iterating `MEASURED_CASES` instead of `cases`; the file after the completeness assertion hashes identical; 130/130 tests in the file at both base and head; head CI at my last read: Test Core 6 of 6 green, every completed check green, `Lint & Repo Gates` still in progress.
- "One row of slack": verified. The base `cases` table has 52 rows against `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(51)`; deleting one row at base reads 129 passed, 0 failed; the same deletion at head is red (`- "tree.labelField"`).
- ⛔ NOT strictly stronger on the floor's own direction (rows silently deleted), measured. Deleting the two hard-coded filter-walk rows (`tabs[0].filter[0].field`, `userFilters.tabs[0].filter[0].field`): base red (50 against 51), head silent (128 passed, 0 failed). Deleting the two bare-name duplicate rows (`columns[0]`, `gantt.tooltipFields[0]`): base red, head silent. The new inline comment discloses the duplicate seam but claims "a row deleted from either table takes its position off the covered set, so the deletion is red", which is false for the three filter-walk rows, and for `tabs[].filter` and `userFilters.tabs[].filter` those rows are the only unknown-name assertions in the two tables (elsewhere in the file those two paths are asserted only for the dotted finding class). On a card whose thesis is comments that claim protection they lack, this is an owed edit: either state in that comment that the three filter-walk rows sit outside the criterion, or assert them (a three-element expected list of the hard-coded walks, which the `positionAsserted` docblock already enumerates in prose).
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (slack, fixed in place): agreed, verified above; no separate card.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (`runtime.js` bundles the rule while `runtime.d.ts` exports none of it): confirmed, 3 against 0 in my counts; `splitting: false` in `packages/lint/tsup.config.ts`; not a defect.
- `out_of_scope_findings[2]` (replaced the fenced inline comment): correct. The card body locates the defect in the docblock and says it is not in the inline comment, which is a statement of where the defect is, not a bar on removing a comment whose assertion is gone. The card's route A removes the floor; a floor comment above an equality would be a false comment of exactly the card's class; the replacement does not call the old comment wrong and was flagged in both the PR body and the report rather than taken silently. The overclaim is in the NEW comment (bullet above), not in the act of replacing.
- Scope fence: `POSITIONS` unchanged (byte-identical); barrel unchanged (0-byte diff); no double assertion (`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` survives only in the comment describing what was replaced, test file line 340).
- Carriers: `needs:contract-review` is on both the card and the PR; the PR is a draft; the PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is the one `check-changeset-no-major` reads and is the seat's to rewrite.
- Owed before landing, at a new head: (a) delete the changeset and apply `skip-changeset` (or `patch` if the seat reads the moved maps as a release; not `minor`); (b) rewrite the PR body's declaration to `Clause-②: no` and correct the "all nine artifacts byte-identical" sentence to the measured 10 of 14; (c) fix the new inline comment's floor-takeover claim for the three filter-walk rows, or assert those walks.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-18836-position-count-floor-overclaims`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
